title: Late Integration Boost data delays payment by a full week, and that delay is the only sanction
content:
A.2.2.9.2.2.1.2.3 fixes both the measurement window and the consequence of missing it: "Data is calculated on a weekly basis from Monday to Sunday for payment the following Monday. Failure to submit data on time will result in a delay of payment of the Integration Boost until the following week."

The sanction is purely a timing penalty. Nothing is forfeited, no eligibility is lost, and no fee is charged — the reward simply arrives a week later. That is a proportionate design for a recurring operational obligation: the party harmed by lateness is the one that was late, and the ecosystem's exposure is unchanged because the underlying balances still qualify.

It also keeps the settlement machinery simple. A forfeiture rule would require adjudicating whose fault the lateness was, which matters here because the submitting party is often not the beneficiary — currently the Core Council Risk Advisor computes the data (A.2.2.9.2.2.1.2.2), and long term it may be a contractor, the partner, the Prime Agent, or Operational GovOps. Penalizing the beneficiary for a third party's lateness would be unjust; a delay affects everyone in the chain equally and self-corrects.

The weekly window also explains why the fastest available distribution Cadence is weekly (A.2.2.9.2.2.1.3.1): payment cannot outpace the data cycle that feeds it.
description: Data is computed Monday-to-Sunday for payment the following Monday; missing the window pushes payment to the next week rather than forfeiting it.
